## Comparison Operators

Remember that these are the Python comparison operator:

| Comparison         | Operator | True example | False Example |
|--------------------|----------|--------------|---------------|
| Less than          | <        | 2 < 3        | 2 < 2         |
| Greater than       | >        | 3>2          | 3>3           |
| Less than or equal | <=       | 2 <= 2       | 3 <= 2        |
| Greater or equal   | >=       | 3 >= 3       | 2 >= 3        |
| Equal              | ==       | 3 == 3       | 3 == 2        |
| Not equal          | !=       | 3 != 2       | 2 != 2        |

When you run the cell below, it will print one 10 questions, one quesstion at a time.

For each question a random number greater than 0 is chosen. 

You will be told the number is between 0 and X (e.g. "between 0 and 20", or "between 0 and 10").

The number will be stored in a variable called something like `variable_1`.

A box will appear where you can use comparison operators to ask Python questions like:

- "Is `variable_1` less than or equal to 7?" - `variable_1 <= 7`

- "Is `variable_1` greater than 3?" - `variable_1 > 3`

Python will answer you with `True` or `False`.

After you use a comparison operator and see whether your question is `True` or `False`, then a new box will appear for you to guess the number.
